topic: dsh-whale-meter: Token Usage Tiers and Cost Dashboard for DSH

key_points: Primary source — 🐳 whale-meter (鲸鱼电表): DeepSeek Harness usage & cost dashboard. One-line install, zero-config, all data local.
Token usage tiers: 🐟 small fry → 🐠 tropical fish → 🐬 dolphin → 🐋 humpback → 🐳 blue whale, with estimated percentile and '≈ N reads of Three-Body' magnitude conversion.
Costs: today/yesterday/month/cumulative in CNY (swappable to USD), estimated from official DeepSeek pricing.
8-17 price-hike compare: same usage priced under old vs new tariff side-by-side; pre-8-17 is a preview, post-8-17 a retroactive back-calculation.
Peak/off-peak (峰谷) billing: from 8-17 peak/off-peak tiers (off-peak is half of peak); badge shows ⚡½ during off-peak.
Cross-price-day correctness: price tables organized by effective date ranges, historical bills not mis-computed.
Cache ledger: hit rate + 'cache saved you ¥X' — more valuable after price hike since hit/miss gap widened.

Multi-vendor pricing: DeepSeek / Anthropic / OpenAI / Google / Zhipu GLM / Moonshot Kimi — 46 models, itemized against official pricing pages; supports China vendors' tiered pricing (GLM-5.1 input <32K ¥6 vs ≥32K ¥8; GLM-4.7 sub-divides by output length).
Privacy: all data on-device (~/.dsh/whale-meter/usage-YYYY-MM.jsonl stores raw tokens only, no amounts frozen); no network requests except optional balance query; no telemetry.
Install: dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-whale-meter; web panel at http://127.0.0.1:3080/whale-meter/api/summary for TUI/headless.
CacheLens — local-first cost tracking proxy for LLM APIs (Show HN).
Focuses on cache-hit cost savings as a proxy-level financial observability layer.
Relevant angle: cache savings are a recurring theme in agent cost optimization.
Agentic Metric — token/cost tracking for AI coding agents (Show HN).
Competitor in the agent token/cost measurement space, broader than DSH-specific.
AgentLedger — SDK-based observability tracking real-world agent actions, not just LLM calls.
Live SSE streaming of every action with sub-second latency.
Competitor framing: ledger-style tracking vs whale-meter's DSH-native plugin approach.
Industry now frames AI spend as a budgeting/control problem; many teams 3x over 2026 token budgets by April.
Real-world incidents: reported $500M Claude bill, engineers with monthly token spikes in the $40,000 range.
Contextualizes why DSH users need token meters like whale-meter.

stats.fact: v4-flash price change on 8-17 (per million tokens, miss): hit ¥0.02→¥0.10 peak, miss ¥1→¥3 peak, output ¥2→¥9 peak; off-peak is exactly half (hit ¥0.05, miss ¥1.5, output ¥4.5).
v4-pro adjusted in parallel (peak ¥0.30 / ¥9 / ¥27; off-peak half). Peak hours are Beijing 9:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00.
Even fully on off-peak, the 8-17 rate is MORE expensive than before 8-17; off-peak is still above the old flat price.
whale-meter covers 46 models across 6 vendors: DeepSeek, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Zhipu GLM, Moonshot Kimi.
China vendor tiered pricing example: GLM-5.1 input <32K tokens costs ¥6, ≥32K costs ¥8 per million; GLM-4.7 sub-divides further by output length.
Whale-meter tracks 5 usage tiers: 🐟 small fry / 🐠 tropical fish / 🐬 dolphin / 🐋 humpback / 🐳 blue whale, with estimated percentile (not claimed as global rank).
Built-in price table version 2026-08-16 already includes the 8-17 new prices; pricing updated via src/pricing.data.ts one-file change + npm run gen:pricing.
Repo: Shiye-10Pages/dsh-whale-meter, TypeScript, MIT License, created 2026-08-16, ~3 stars, default branch main.

angles: Why DSH (DeepSeek Harness) users need a token meter now — the 8-17 price hike made cost visibility a budgeting necessity.
Peak/off-peak billing is a NEW cost lever: off-peak is half price but still above the old flat rate — a nuanced, non-obvious point most guides get wrong.
Privacy-first design: fully local, no telemetry, raw-token-only storage (amounts recomputed) vs cloud dashboards — a trust differentiator.
China-tiered pricing (GLM <32K vs ≥32K) is a complexity most cost tools ignore; whale-meter handles it per-call.
Gamified tiers + shareable score card ('≈ N reads of Three-Body') as an engagement/retention angle.
Comparison: DSH-native plugin (zero-config) vs generic proxy/ledger tools (CacheLens, AgentLedger, Agentic Metric).
Cache hit-rate economics post-price-hike: cache savings widen because hit/miss gap scaled up.
